articles.title: Simone Biles reveals the surprising relationship she has with an influencer
articles.standfirst: A simple request about a hairstylist ended with the Olympic champion deciding to hit unfollow
articles.summary: A simple request about a hairstylist ended with the Olympic champion deciding to hit unfollow
articles.body:
Simone Biles has never been shy about discussing the pressures that come with being one of the world's most recognizable athletes.

But in a recent story, the Olympic champion revealed an unexpectedly awkward relationship with an influencer that had nothing to do with gymnastics , and everything to do with hair.

Biles opened up about what she described as the “weirdest interaction” she had with an influencer a couple of years ago. The gymnast explained that she had followed the woman for some time because she admired her style and content, particularly the way she wore her hair.

The detail that caught Biles ' attention was how consistently polished the influencer's hairstyle appeared. Biles said it was always “laid to a T,” leaving her unsure whether the look was her natural hair or a weave.

At the time, Biles was particularly conscious about her own hair because of the criticism she had received online. That scrutiny had become a recurring issue throughout her career, including during major competitions.

“I didn’t really give a f**k that much. Y’all had been bullying me for so long about what my hair looked like during competition,” she recalled.

The criticism had nevertheless made Biles consider whether changing her hairstyle might quiet some of the comments. Because she already had conversations with the influencer about hair and had regularly complimented her looks, she felt comfortable asking for the contact details of her stylist.

“Girl, you need to send me your hair person contact slash Insta,” Biles recalled asking.

The response was not what she expected. According to Biles, the influencer told her, “My manager has it. I’ll have to ask her.”

That answer left the gymnast confused. She questioned why someone would not have the direct details of the person responsible for their hair.

“You don’t know who does your hair when you go to your hair appointments? You don’t have their contact or Instagram?” she asked in the video.

Biles acknowledged that she could understand someone wanting to protect a stylist's information. However, she said that was not what she had in mind.

“That’s not at all what it was, like I travel all the time, so if I’m ever in that area, let me get slay,” she said.

Rather than pursuing the matter, Biles ultimately decided that the interaction was not worth the negativity.

“But yeah, I didn’t need that kind of negativity in my life, so I unfollowed her,” Biles said.

Why hair has become such a personal subject for Biles

The incident was amusing enough for Biles to revisit years later, but it also connects to a much more serious part of her relationship with public scrutiny.

Biles has repeatedly faced criticism over her hair despite becoming one of the most decorated gymnasts in history. During the 2024 Paris Olympics, for example, she responded directly to social-media users who criticized her hairstyle.

She explained that the extreme heat and lengthy bus journey had affected her appearance before competition.

Her experiences have also shaped the way she views her natural hair. In a 2024 interview with Elle, Biles explained that she had gradually become more comfortable with her texture and the styles she could wear: “I used to worry about [my hair being considered] not professional. But I’m not embarrassed about it anymore.”

She has also spoken about growing up without learning to style her own hair, meaning professional hairstylists became an important part of her routine as her gymnastics career developed.

That history makes the influencer story particularly revealing. What started as Biles simply admiring another woman's hairstyle was connected to years of being told, directly and indirectly, how her own appearance should look.

Biles has previously argued that the scrutiny surrounding Black women's hair can become excessive. During the Paris Olympics, she famously pushed back against critics, telling them not to comment on a Black woman's hair while she was competing.

Her relationship with hair has continued to evolve away from trying to satisfy those expectations. More recently, she has also worked with K18 as a brand ambassador, with the partnership focusing on maintaining healthy hair despite the demands of training, traveling and performing.

The influencer episode therefore represents a lighter chapter in a much bigger story. Biles was not looking for anything complicated, she admired someone's hair, wanted the stylist's contact information and thought it could be useful when traveling.

Instead, the answer surprised her enough that she chose to walk away from the relationship. Years later, she still remembers the exchange.

“To this day, I still think about it, and it cracks me up, but it also like, what?” she said.

For someone who has spent much of her life under an extraordinary level of public scrutiny, the story is another example of Biles deciding which conversations deserve her attention, and which ones are better left behind.

articles.title: Simone Biles asked a simple question and got an answer she never expected
articles.standfirst: The Olympic legend admired the influencer and only wanted one simple favor, but the response was enough for Biles to unfollow her
articles.summary: The Olympic legend admired the influencer and only wanted one simple favor, but the response was enough for Biles to unfollow her
articles.body:
S imone Biles has dealt with pressure on the biggest stages in sports, but years later, one surprisingly small interaction with an influencer still leaves her wondering what exactly happened.

The 29-year-old gymnastics legend took to TikTok to tell the story of what she described as one of the "weirdest" interactions she has ever had with an influencer and how a simple question about hair eventually convinced her to hit the unfollow button.

Biles explained that the two had followed each other on social media for some time. She liked the woman's style and content, but there was one thing that particularly caught her attention: her hair always looked perfect.

And for Biles, that wasn't just about appearance.

Simone Biles explains why hair became such a sensitive subject

Throughout her career, Biles has faced relentless comments about her hair while competing, something she directly referenced while telling the story.

"Y'all have been bullying me for so long about what my hair looks like during competition," Biles said, explaining why she had become particularly interested in finding someone who could help her achieve the look she wanted.

That criticism wasn't something Biles imagined. During the Paris Olympics in 2024, she publicly responded to people commenting on her hair after competing with a ponytail, explaining that extreme heat and a long bus ride without air conditioning had affected how it looked.

So when Biles saw the influencer repeatedly posting photos with what she considered flawless hair, she eventually decided to ask.

The two had already exchanged messages about their hair when another Instagram Story gave Biles the opportunity. She complimented the influencer and asked for the contact information or Instagram account of the person who did her hair.

The response was not what she expected.

The answer that made Simone Biles say 'What?'

According to Biles, the influencer replied that her manager had the hairstylist's information and that she would have to ask her . Biles couldn't understand it.

"You don't know who does your hair when you go to your hair appointments?" she recalled thinking.

For Biles, it felt like unnecessary gatekeeping. She also pointed out that the two women didn't even live in the same state, making the idea that she might somehow take the influencer's hairstylist away from her even harder to understand.

Biles said her intention was much simpler. Because she travels frequently, she wanted the contact so she could potentially get her hair done whenever she happened to be in that area.

But she wasn't going to push the issue.

"I didn't need that kind of negativity in my life, so I unfollowed her," Biles said.

Years later, Biles still doesn't know whether the influencer was actually trying to protect her hairstylist, simply didn't have the contact information or whether there was another explanation entirely.

She only knows that the answer felt strange enough at the time to make her walk away. And apparently, strange enough that she still laughs about it today.

articles.title: "Why Not?": Jordan Chiles enlists Michael Jordan for epic LA 2028 comeback announcement
articles.standfirst: The Team USA star has ended months of uncertainty and confirmed she is chasing a third Games
articles.summary: The Team USA star has ended months of uncertainty and confirmed she is chasing a third Games
articles.body:
Jordan Chiles spent much of the past year refusing to rush the biggest decision of her gymnastics career. Now she has made it.

The two-time Olympian has confirmed she plans to pursue a place on Team USA for the 2028 Los Angeles Games , setting up the possibility of a third Olympic appearance four years after the medal controversy that overshadowed the end of her Paris campaign.

Chiles revealed the decision in a stylized announcement filmed in Los Angeles, with model Winnie Harlow and singer Normani appearing alongside her and Michael Jordan providing the voiceover.

“Why again? Because the dream is still there. Why continue? Because there’s still more to give,” Jordan says in the video. “Why now? Because not every chapter ends when people expect it to.”

He then asks why Chiles would return for a third attempt. Her answer is immediate: “Why not?” The 25-year-old completes the reveal by showing off a jeweled grill reading “LA 2028.”

Chiles deliberately kept Olympic future open

The announcement ends months of uncertainty around whether Chiles would continue at the elite level after completing her college career with UCLA.

Earlier this year, she made clear that another Olympic run would only happen if she felt physically and mentally ready.

“The biggest thing right now is just making sure my body and my mind are okay,” Chiles said. “I did give myself a deadline on when I would decide. So it’s not a yes, it’s not a no.”

That careful approach followed an extraordinary stretch in which Chiles balanced NCAA gymnastics, television appearances and the aftermath of the Paris Olympics.

At UCLA, she finished as a four-time NCAA champion and 23-time All-American before transitioning into a student coaching role for the 2027 season. Her elite resume is already substantial.

Chiles won team silver at the Tokyo Olympics and team gold in Paris, while also collecting World Championship medals and becoming one of the most recognizable figures in American gymnastics.

Paris medal battle still hangs over career

The most painful chapter of Chiles ’ Olympic story remains unresolved. She was initially awarded bronze in the floor exercise final in Paris after a U.S. scoring inquiry raised her mark.

Romania successfully challenged the timing of that inquiry, and Chiles was later ordered to return the medal.

The case has continued through the Swiss legal system, with Switzerland’s highest court directing the Court of Arbitration for Sport to reconsider the dispute after new audiovisual evidence was presented.

“This case is bigger than one competition or one result,” Chiles later wrote. “It is about trust.”

That experience could have made Paris feel like a natural endpoint. Instead, Chiles is choosing to write another chapter. With Los Angeles hosting the next Summer Games, the opportunity carries a different weight.

Suni Lee, Jade Carey and Hezly Rivera have also signaled their intention to pursue 2028, potentially setting up another fiercely competitive U.S. selection process. Chiles , however, has already answered the first question. She is coming back.
